column3: Sample Take Home Pay Policies
Minimum Take‑Home Pay Based on Basic Salary (employee group assignment)
Employees must receive not less than 40% of their basic salary after all payroll deductions per payroll cycle.
Sample Rules:
Mandatory statutory deductions (SSS, PhilHealth, Pag‑IBIG, WHT) shall be applied in full.
Company loans, cooperative loans, salary advances, and optional deductions may be reduced or deferred to preserve the minimum take‑home pay.
Any deferred deductions shall be carried over to the succeeding payroll cycles.
HR/Payroll shall notify employees when deductions are deferred.
Take‑Home Pay Guarantee on Gross Pay (employee group assignment)

Employees must receive at least 30% of their total gross pay (basic pay + allowances + OT + premiums + de minimis + reimbursements/receivables + absences + tardiness + undertime + bonus + other earnings).
Sample Rules:
All statutory deductions shall still apply in full.
If optional deductions exceed allowable limits, they will be automatically prorated or deferred.
Deductions with existing repayment schedules (e.g., company loans) must be reprioritized to comply with the minimum THP rule.
Take‑Home Pay Guarantee on Gross Pay Less Reimbursements/Receivables (employee group assignment)
Employees must receive at least 30% of their total gross pay less reimbursements/receivables (gross pay - reimbursements/receivables).
Sample Rules:
All statutory deductions shall still apply in full.
If optional deductions exceed allowable limits, they will be automatically prorated or deferred.
Deductions with existing repayment schedules (e.g., company loans) must be reprioritized to comply with the minimum THP rule.
Guaranteed Minimum Net Pay Policy (employee group assignment)
All employees must take home not less than ₱8,000 net pay per pay period
Sample Rules:
Applies equally to daily‑paid, monthly‑paid, probationary, and regular employees.
Non‑essential deductions (e.g., meal charges, gym dues, social club fees) are deprioritized.
HRIS must automatically defer low‑priority deductions when net pay risks falling below the guaranteed minimum.
Guaranteed Minimum Net Pay Policy (employee group assignment)
All employees must take home not less than ₱0.00 net pay per pay period
Sample Rules:
Applies equally to daily‑paid, monthly‑paid, probationary, and regular employees.
Non‑essential deductions (e.g., meal charges, gym dues, social club fees) are deprioritized.
HRIS must automatically defer low‑priority deductions when net pay risks falling below the guaranteed minimum.
Sample Rule on Loan Deduction Cap With Take‑Home Protection (employee group assignment)
Total loan repayments may not exceed 25% of the employee’s gross salary unless expressly approved by the Approver.
Sample Rules:
All loan deductions (company, bank, cooperative) are combined for computation.
If the total exceeds 25%, excess loan repayments shall be restructured.
Ensures that the employee’s take‑home pay remains adequate for living needs.

Sample Rules:

Sample Rule on Lates, Absences, Undertime Cap With Take‑Home Protection (employee group assignment)
Total LAABS and Undertime deduction may not exceed 25% of the employee’s gross salary unless expressly approved by the Approver.
Sample Rules:
All LAABS and undertime are combined for computation.
If the total exceeds 25%, excess LAABS and Undertime shall be deferred for deduction.
Ensures that the employee’s take‑home pay remains adequate for living needs.

Sample Rules:

Sample Rule on Lates, Absences, Undertime Cap With Take‑Home Protection (employee group assignment)
Total LAABS and Undertime deduction should not result in a net pay lower than the protected minimum unless expressly approved by the Approver.
Sample Rules:
All LAABS and undertime are combined for computation.

If the total results in a net pay lower than the protected minimum, excess LAABS and Undertime shall be deferred for deduction. The system will automatically adjust the number of LAABS and Undertime to meet the minimum take home pay requirement
Ensures that the employee’s take‑home pay remains adequate for living needs.
Sample Rule on Hierarchy of Deductions/Loans and Take‑Home Safeguard (employee group assignment)
To ensure fair deduction management, the following order of hierarchy (what will be the first item to be adjusted) applies:.

Please take note different scenarios and setup: (1) Adjust the amount of the 1st rank. If the 1st rank adjustment will cause the net pay amount to meet the percentage or amount required take home pay, the system doesn't need to adjust/deduct the full amount, only adjust upto the amount needed to meet the requirement. (2) Adjust the amount of the 1st rank. If the 1st rank adjustment will not yet meet the percentage or amount required take home pay, the system will adjust the 2nd rank, and apply and adjust the sequence or order until the employee's minimum take home pay is reached. (3) Deduct the full amount of the 1st rank. If the 1st rank adjustment will cause the net pay amount to meet the percentage or amount required take home pay, the system doesn't need to deduct the full amount of the next ranks.

Compute gross income
Apply all statutory deductions
Apply prioritized deductions
Set priorities or hierarchy so:
Statutory deductions are always deducted
High-priority company/government deductions or loans are deducted is possible
Low-priority company/government deductions or loans are trimmed, reduced, or skipped
Run the take home pay threshold check
Is the net pay equals or more than the required minimum?
If yes, payroll posts normally
If no, system reduces, prorates, or defers lower-priority deductions until the minimum net pay is reached

Possible Computation Steps:
Determine daily rate
Determine 22.5 day equivalent (22.5 x daily rate = 1/2 monthly salary equivalent)
Multiply by years of service - fractions equal or more than 6 months count as 1 full year
Retirement pay = Daily rate x 22.5 x years of service
Integrate/Add to the final pay computation
